question.text: Per Chapter 6, GST on AIF fees is typically NOT recoverable as Input Tax Credit by the fund because:

answer.text: AIFs do not provide taxable output services, and so cannot claim input credit on their fees
GST on AIF fees is reverse-charged
AIFs are always registered as SEZ units
GST does not apply at all to AIFs

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 6 (section 6.3.4): 'AIFs do not provide any services and therefore do not necessarily collect GST on output services. The absence of recoverability of indirect tax such as GST increases the cost for investors in the fund.' **The Trap:** B misapplies reverse charge; C is false; D is false (GST DOES apply on fees). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers this. Same ITC-non-recoverability applies to most mutual funds and PMSes too — structural feature of the service-service chain. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Factor 36 bps (18% x 2% fee) + GST on trustee/admin/legal into your LP return model. Don't promise 'net 2% fee' if the all-in is 2.4-2.6% — LPs do the math and will call you on the discrepancy.
